item.title: ECB set to hike as Iran war fuels fresh inflation fears
item.description: The European Central Bank looks set to raise interest rates on Thursday for the second time this year, seeking to head off an energy-driven surge in inflation triggered by the Iran war.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Canepa, Balazs Koranyi
item.content:encoded: The European Central Bank looks set to raise interest rates on Thursday for the second time this year, seeking to head off an energy-driven surge in inflation triggered by the Iran war. Attacks by both sides since the end of August have shattered a month of relative calm, with the [USN:L6N451042 TEXT:"U.S. and Iran"] hitting military, shipping and energy assets. That has sent [USN:L1N451087 TEXT:"oil and gas prices"] soaring again and revived fears about a wave of price hikes in the fuel-importing euro zone. [USN:L6N44V0GE TEXT:"Economists expect"] the ECB to respond by raising its policy rate to 2.50% from 2.25% on Thursday and [USN:L1N44O0IZ TEXT:"signalling"] it is ready to tighten further if the inflation outlook does not improve. "A September hike looks all but locked in," Alessia Berardi, head of global macroeconomics at the Amundi Investment Institute, said. "Inflation remains elevated and should stay sticky over the next few months before easing toward the second half of next year." RESILIENT ECONOMY PROVIDES COMFORT ECB President Christine Lagarde and colleagues, this month gathering in Berlin for their annual venture away from the central bank's headquarters, are likely to take comfort from [USN:APNAAEW17 TEXT:"recent growth data"]. The 21-country euro zone economy has been [USN:ZRN00EJAM TEXT:"holding up"] better than anticipated despite [USN:L1N43X0G1 TEXT:"higher fuel costs"], competition from China and the impact of [USN:L1N44H0BO TEXT:"droughts"]. Bank lending even [USN:APNA5EE1M TEXT:"picked up pace"] in July, suggesting the ECB's June rate rise had not yet dented activity and giving policymakers scope to tighten further if needed. "We expect President Lagarde to maintain a hawkish wait-and-see stance, leaving the door open to further tightening," Martin Wolburg, senior economist at Generali Investments, said. Financial markets are pricing in another two or three hikes by the end of next year. Financing conditions have already tightened as long-term bond yields [USN:L6N4500RP TEXT:"scale highs"] not seen since before the global financial crisis, reflecting inflation concerns and worries about ballooning government debt. Competition from bond sales by big tech companies aggressively raising money to fund the AI boom, and [USN:L8N44Y0C9 TEXT:"political turmoil"] in Germany, have added to upward pressure on yields. ECB TO RAISE GROWTH AND INFLATION PROJECTIONS On Thursday, the ECB is also expected to raise its growth projections for this year, and possibly 2027, reflecting the economy's staying power. But it may push back the timeline for inflation — now above 3% — to return to its 2% target. In June, the bank had pencilled that in for next summer. Thursday's forecasts are unlikely to fully capture the latest energy-price surge, however, with Brent crude having touched $100 a barrel on Wednesday. Lorenzo Codogno, founder of LC Macro Advisors, said higher fuel costs, trade tensions and weather-related disruptions were creating conditions for another rise in inflation, potentially forcing the ECB to tighten again in October and December. "We may now be at an inflation turning point, and wages will also show upward pressure at some point," Codogno said. BURDEN OF PROOF IS ON THE DATA So far, the key indicators the ECB watches have broadly been benign. Core inflation, which strips out energy and food prices, [USN:L1N44T095 TEXT:"eased"] to 2.4% last month and the latest survey showed consumers [USN:L1N44I07X TEXT:"had trimmed"] their expectations for price growth. Pay rises had also [USN:L8N44I0DA TEXT:"moderated"]. But analysts at Barclays cautioned that inflationary pressure was quietly building beneath the surface, with core goods prices gaining momentum and producer prices rising far faster than consumer prices. "This leaves core goods inflation on a firmer footing and provides a higher base from which we expect the inflationary effects of the Middle East conflict to build over the quarters ahead," they wrote in a note. Carsten Brzeski, global head of macro at ING, said that companies — at least in Germany — had so far absorbed the higher costs, in marked contrast to 2022, when the energy shock following Russia's invasion of Ukraine unleashed a broad inflationary surge. LAGARDE LIKELY TO FACE QUESTIONS ON HER OWN FUTURE Beyond the rate decision, Lagarde is likely to be asked at her post-decision press conference about her own tenure, which is scheduled to run until October 31, 2027. The ECB chief has repeatedly been linked to the leadership of the World Economic Forum, and [USN:L1N43B0U3 TEXT:"spoke in July"] of her desire to champion European values in some capacity during the campaign for next year's French presidential election. Pressed later that month on whether that meant leaving the ECB early, she merely said: "You are not going to see the back of me before 2027." A [USN:L8N44V0O7 TEXT:"report last week"] suggesting that ECB board member Isabel Schnabel was in talks to join the International Monetary Fund could herald a reshuffle at the top of the euro zone's central bank.

item.title: Tigers snap 7-series losing skid at Twins' expense
item.description: Colt Keith hit a two-run homer in the first inning and the host Detroit Tigers never looked back, rolling to a 7-2 win over the Minnesota Twins on Wednesday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Colt Keith hit a two-run homer in the first inning and the host Detroit Tigers never looked back, rolling to a 7-2 win over the Minnesota Twins on Wednesday afternoon. Keith's long ball was his 10th of the season. The Tigers (67-79) snapped their seven-series losing streak since Aug. 14-16 by taking two of three games from Minnesota. Dillon Dingler drove in two runs, while John Peck scored a run and drove in another. Hao-Yu Lee walked three times and scored twice. Detroit starter Keider Montero gave up two runs in four innings. He was taken out due to the birth of his child. Left-hander Tyler Holton (2-5) didn't allow a baserunner while recording two strikeouts in two innings and collected the victory. Kody Clemens and Josh Bell homered for the Twins (69-77). Twins starter Zebby Matthews (9-10) lasted just 2 1/3 innings. The right-hander gave up five runs on two hits and four walks while fanning two. The Tigers jumped to a two-run lead in the first inning. Lee drew a one-out walk before Keith deposited a Matthews changeup over the right field wall. Keith also hit his first homer of the season off Matthews on June 11 in Detroit. Detroit stretched its lead to 5-0 in the third. Peck walked and moved to third on Kevin McGonigle's double to left. Lee walked to load the bases. Matthews struck out Keith but then walked Riley Greene to force in a run. Matthews was removed in favor of Travis Adams. Dingler's sacrifice fly to left allowed McGonigle to score and Brett Callahan's ground-rule double scored Lee. Minnesota got two runs back in the fourth as Clemens and Bell hit back-to-back homers. Detroit made it 6-2 in the seventh with a two-out run. Spencer Torkelson singled and Greene drew another walk before Dingler's single brought in Torkelson. The Tigers tacked on another run in the eighth. Max Clark walked, stole second, advanced to third on a groundout and scored on Peck's single. --Field Level Media

item.title: Anec vê avanço na exportação de soja do Brasil em setembro e recorde para farelo
item.description: A exportação de soja do Brasil em setembro foi estimada nesta quarta-feira em 7,74 milhões de toneladas, crescimento de cerca de 760 mil toneladas em relação ao mesmo período do ano passado, de acordo com a primeira projeção de embarques da Associação Nacional dos Exportadores de Cereais (Anec) para o mês.
item.dc:creator: Roberto Samora
item.content:encoded: A exportação de soja do Brasil em setembro foi estimada nesta quarta-feira em 7,74 milhões de toneladas, crescimento de cerca de 760 mil toneladas em relação ao mesmo período do ano passado, de acordo com a primeira projeção de embarques da Associação Nacional dos Exportadores de Cereais (Anec) para o mês. Já a exportação de milho deverá registrar nova queda no mês na comparação com o mesmo período do ano passado, para 5,2 milhões de toneladas, versus quase 7 milhões em setembro de 2025. Enquanto as exportações de soja do Brasil vêm sendo embaladas por demanda firme e uma safra recorde, no milho o país enfrenta maior concorrência de países como Argentina e EUA este ano. Exportadores ainda lidam com uma disputa do mercado interno, especialmente do setor de etanol, enquanto fazendeiros têm segurado o produto. A Anec destacou que as exportações de soja em agosto fecharam em 9,6 milhões de toneladas e as de milho somaram 5 milhões de toneladas. Com base nos volumes embarcados no ano e nas projeções iniciais para setembro, a Anec estimou que as exportações de soja no acumulado dos nove primeiros meses do ano deverão somar 102 milhões de toneladas, volume já próximo do recorde anual registrado em 2025, de 108,68 milhões de toneladas. No caso do milho, a projeção de embarques até o final de setembro é de 19,35 milhões de toneladas, menos da metade das 41,59 milhões de 2025 completo. A Anec não fez considerações sobre projeções de embarques para a soja no ano. Anteriormente, estimou um recorde de 110 milhões de toneladas para 2026. No milho, a entidade citou projeção da S&P Global Energy, que indica 39 milhões de toneladas do cereal exportadas pelo país no atual ano comercial. A associação lembrou ainda que, nos últimos meses do ano, a exportação de soja tem um "comportamento sazonal" e abre espaço para o escoamento da segunda safra de milho. "A atividade comercial ganhou força na segunda metade de agosto, com cooperativas apontando maior participação de tradings e usinas de etanol de milho na disputa pela oferta oriunda da safrinha", apontou o relatório, admitindo que anteriormente os volumes exportados foram menores pela retenção do cereal colhido, da maior atratividade do mercado físico e da margem de exportação apertada. FARELO RECORDE A Anec estimou as exportações de farelo de soja em 2,6 milhões de toneladas em setembro, aumento de 673 mil toneladas no comparativo anual, o que colocaria o volume no maior patamar mensal do ano. O total também superaria recorde histórico verificado em maio deste ano. Conforme o relatório, o contexto do mercado favorece o fortalecimento dos prêmios de exportação de farelo de soja no porto de Paranaguá e estimula negociações para embarques do quarto trimestre. "O suporte também veio do mercado internacional. Preocupações com a safra dos Estados Unidos ajudaram a sustentar os contratos futuros na Bolsa de Chicago, reforçando o viés positivo para os preços FOB sul-americanos." No ano até setembro, as exportações de farelo de soja do Brasil deverão superar 20 milhões de toneladas, a caminho de ultrapassar o recorde de 23 milhões de toneladas de 2025, apontou a Anec.

item.title: Presupuesto de Colombia para 2027 muestra profundo desequilibrio y requiere esfuerzo significativo: Fitch
item.description: El presupuesto de gastos de Colombia para el próximo año muestra un profundo desequilibrio y requiere un esfuerzo de ajuste significativo, dijo el miércoles la agencia calificadora de riesgos Fitch.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El presupuesto de gastos de Colombia para el próximo año muestra un profundo desequilibrio y requiere un esfuerzo de ajuste significativo, dijo el miércoles la agencia calificadora de riesgos Fitch. El Ministerio de Hacienda presentó la semana pasada al Congreso un proyecto de presupuesto de gastos para 2027 por 634,9 billones de pesos (201.922 millones de dólares), en el que elevó la proyección de déficit fiscal para ese año hasta un 9,4% del Producto Interno Bruto (PIB), frente a una de 4,5% esperada anteriormente y aumentó sus necesidades de deuda. El déficit fiscal del próximo año previsto por el Gobierno es superior a la proyección del 5,8% del PIB estimado previamente por Fitch. La agencia consideró que aun cuando el Gobierno plantea presentar una ley fiscal de "rescate" para recortar el gasto público en 2027 y logre un ajuste equivalente a un 2,2% del PIB, "es probable que los déficits superen considerablemente las proyecciones anteriores de Fitch". Además, para este año el Gobierno subió su objetivo de déficit fiscal a un 7,2% del PIB, desde uno previo de 5,3%. La calificadora mencionó que serían necesarios esfuerzos adicionales para estabilizar la deuda de Colombia, al tiempo que obtener financiación de la magnitud que plantea el Gobierno en los mercados de bonos resultaría difícil y requeriría apoyo sustancial de instituciones financieras internacionales. "Aunque las autoridades implementen medidas para reducir la brecha presupuestaria, es probable que esta sea sustancialmente superior a la estimación previa de Fitch, situando a la deuda en una trayectoria ascendente más pronunciada", advirtió. Fitch aseguró que la falta de implementación de medidas de consolidación fiscal podría ejercer nuevas presiones sobre la calificación crediticia del país sudamericano. La calificadora dijo que el país podría requerir un ajuste mayor a los 4 puntos porcentuales del PIB que había estimado la firma anteriormente para estabilizar la relación deuda/PIB "dada la situación de partida más desfavorable identificada por el nuevo gobierno".

item.title: Cooper Companies cuts annual profit forecast on weak contact lens demand
item.description: Cooper Companies lowered its annual profit forecast on Wednesday and posted third-quarter revenue below Wall Street estimates, as weak demand for its contact lenses weighed on sales.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Cooper Companies (COO.O) lowered its annual profit forecast on Wednesday and posted third-quarter revenue below Wall Street estimates, as weak demand for its contact lenses weighed on sales. Shares of the San Roman, California-based company fell about 15% in extended trading. Here are more details: Cooper now expects annual adjusted profit per share of $4.51 to $4.55, compared with its prior forecast of $4.58 to $4.66 The company also trimmed its forecast for fiscal 2026 revenue to a range of $4.23 billion to $4.25 billion, from its prior view of $4.29 billion to $4.32 billion Analysts on average expect 2026 revenue of $4.31 billion and profit of $4.63 per share, according to data compiled by LSEG. Cooper completed a [USN:L4N3XA1LY TEXT:"strategic review"] that included evaluating a potential sale of its CooperSurgical unit, but its board unanimously decided to retain the business. For the third quarter, revenue came in at $1.07 billion, below analysts' average estimate of $1.10 billion. Cooper posted a quarterly adjusted profit of $1.15 per share surpassing estimates of $1.12. Cooper increased its share repurchase authorization to $3 billion from $2 billion. The medical device maker expects fourth-quarter revenue of $1.06 billion to $1.08 billion and adjusted per-share profit of $1.05 to $1.09. CooperVision, the company's contact lens business, reported third-quarter revenue of $717 million for the period ended July 31, down from $723.5 million in the previous quarter. A reduction in U.S. channel inventory weighed on results and is expected to continue affecting the next quarter.

item.title: S&P 500 fecha em baixa, com petróleo ultrapassando US$100 por barril
item.description: As ações nos EUA fecharam em baixa nesta quarta-feira, com os preços do petróleo disparando para mais de US$100 por barril, enquanto os papéis da Apple caíram e os rendimentos dos títulos do Tesouro subiram antes da divulgação de dados cruciais sobre a inflação, previstos para o final da semana.
item.dc:creator: Noel Randewich, Tharuniyaa Lakshmi
item.content:encoded: As ações nos EUA fecharam em baixa nesta quarta-feira, com os preços do petróleo disparando para mais de US$100 por barril, enquanto os papéis da Apple caíram e os rendimentos dos títulos do Tesouro subiram antes da divulgação de dados cruciais sobre a inflação, previstos para o final da semana. Preocupações com o abastecimento global de petróleo e o recrudescimento das tensões no Oriente Médio empurraram o petróleo Brent para acima de US$100 por barril, um nível sensível para o mercado de ações. A guerra dos EUA e de Israel contra o Irã, agora em seu sétimo mês, tem gerado temores de um conflito regional mais amplo, com os altos preços do petróleo alimentando a inflação. O índice de energia do S&P 500 (.SPNY) subiu 1,1%, enquanto todos os outros índices setoriais caíram. A Apple (AAPL.O) encerrou o dia com queda de 0,3% após realizar seu primeiro lançamento de smartphone sob o comando do novo presidente-executivo, John Ternus. O rendimento dos títulos do Tesouro dos EUA de 10 anos, referência do mercado, subiu para o nível mais alto desde novembro de 2023, depois que o Departamento do Tesouro anunciou que compraria até US$6 bilhões em títulos públicos de 10 a 20 anos. Alguns analistas esperavam uma compra maior, na faixa de US$8 bilhões a US$10 bilhões. Rendimentos mais altos em títulos públicos sem risco tornam menos atraente para os investidores manter ações. “Isso está deixando os mercados um pouco preocupados, especialmente porque não temos muitas informações em termos de expectativas de lucros até começarmos a entrar na temporada de divulgação dos resultados do terceiro trimestre”, disse Rob Haworth, estrategista sênior de investimentos do U.S. Bank Wealth Management, em Seattle. Os dados do Índice de Preços ao Produtor dos EUA, na quinta-feira, e os dados dos preços ao consumidor, na sexta-feira, estarão em foco para fornecer pistas sobre a trajetória das taxas de juros do Federal Reserve. Os operadores estão precificando uma chance de 60% de que o Fed aumente as taxas de juros em sua reunião de política monetária na próxima semana. O S&P 500 recuou 0,48%, encerrando o pregão em 7.636,46 pontos. O Nasdaq perdeu 0,64%, para 26.253,34 pontos, enquanto o Dow Jones Industrial Average caiu 0,77%, para 52.381,02 pontos. A Meta (META.O) subiu mais de 6% e limitou a queda do S&P 500 depois que a empresa de mídia social lançou um assistente de IA há muito anunciado, capaz de enviar emails de forma autônoma, vender um carro ou fazer reservas de viagens em nome dos usuários. A Alphabet (GOOGL.O) recuou 2,3% depois que a controladora do Google anunciou que investirá pelo menos US$15,1 bilhões em infraestrutura de IA na Finlândia nos próximos dois anos, incluindo um grande acordo para o fornecimento de energia nuclear. O Índice Philadelphia Semiconductor (.SOX) subiu 0,37%, com a Advanced Micro Devices (AMD.O) registrando alta de 3%.

item.title: Report: Raiders TE Brock Bowers (knee) expected to miss 1-2 games
item.description: Las Vegas Raiders star tight end Brock Bowers underwent a meniscus trim this week and is expected to miss one or two games, ESPN and the NFL Network co-reported on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Las Vegas Raiders star tight end Brock Bowers underwent a meniscus trim this week and is expected to miss one or two games, ESPN and the NFL Network co-reported on Wednesday. Bowers, 23, had the procedure on Tuesday in Dallas for a knee injury that occurred during training camp but wasn't diagnosed until last week, according to the report. A two-time Pro Bowl selection, Bowers was slowed by injuries last season. He dealt with a posterior cruciate ligament issue and a bone bruise in his left knee from the 2025 season opener against New England and still played three games before sitting out the next three. He was placed on injured reserve for the final two weeks of the season and finished with 64 receptions for 680 yards and seven touchdowns in 12 games (eight starts). Las Vegas selected Bowers in the first round (13th overall) in the 2024 NFL Draft out of Georgia. He made the All-Pro first team as a rookie with 112 catches for 1,194 yards and five TDs in 17 games (16 starts). Also, second-year running back Ashton Jeanty returned to practice Wednesday for the first time since injuring his right ankle on Aug. 23. He was hurt when he landed awkwardly while diving for a low pass from quarterback Kirk Cousins. Jeanty rushed for 975 yards and totaled 1,321 scrimmage yards last season as a rookie. He was the No. 6 overall pick in the 2025 draft out of Boise State. The Raiders host the Miami Dolphins on Sunday and visit the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 2. --Field Level Media

item.title: US FDA reports 22 cases of salmonella infections linked to broccoli sprouts
item.description: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration said on Wednesday it was investigating a multistate outbreak of salmonella infections linked to broccoli sprouts, the latest in a series of foodborne-illness investigations involving produce.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration said on Wednesday it was investigating a multistate outbreak of salmonella infections linked to broccoli sprouts, the latest in a series of foodborne-illness investigations involving produce. This comes amidst an ongoing [USN:L1N44W0OG TEXT:"cyclosporiasis"] outbreak linked to lettuce and separate salmonella outbreaks tied to [USN:L4N44G1SR TEXT:"jalapenos"] and [USN:L4N44I122 TEXT:"alfalfa sprouts"] that have shaken U.S. consumer confidence, with many forgoing eating fresh produce or dining out at restaurants. Here are some details: The Food and Drug Administration and Centers for Disease Control and Prevention reported 22 cases of salmonella infections across four states, including two hospitalizations. No cases of deaths were reported. The health agencies said traceback data shows Evergreen Fresh Sprouts in Moyie Springs, Idaho, as the common grower of broccoli sprouts that were eaten by patients before they fell ill. On September 4, Evergreen Fresh Sprouts had initiated a recall of broccoli sprouts based on a positive salmonella result from a sample, collected and analyzed by Montana state officials. The FDA said of the 19 people interviewed, all reported eating sprouts and 17 among them had specifically eaten broccoli sprouts. The health regulator said consumers, restaurants, and retailers should not eat, serve, or sell recalled broccoli sprouts grown by Evergreen Fresh Sprouts. Salmonella is a type of bacteria that can cause food poisoning leading to diarrhea, fever, and abdominal cramps. Broccoli sprouts are broccoli seeds germinated in water for roughly 4 to 6 days and eaten whole.

item.title: U.S. overhauls Ryder Cup qualifying to emphasize recent results
item.description: The United States is overhauling its qualification system for the 2027 Ryder Cup, eliminating the previous year's results and moving away from a points structure tied to prize money.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The United States is overhauling its qualification system for the 2027 Ryder Cup, eliminating the previous year's results and moving away from a points structure tied to prize money. The PGA of America announced Wednesday that the race for six automatic spots on captain Jim Furyk's team will not begin until The American Express tournament in January 2027. Qualifying will span 31 events and conclude following the BMW Championship in August. Under previous systems, performances in select tournaments during the year before a Ryder Cup, including the majors and Players Championship, contributed toward the points standings in addition to current-year performance. That won't be the case this time. "I have worked diligently with our team and am pleased to implement a new qualifying process for the 2027 U.S. Ryder Cup Team," Furyk said. "We possess an exceptional mix of veterans and rising stars, and this system will help us identify the strongest players in September 2027." The revamped formula assigns fixed point values based on each tournament's strength rather than on the amount of money earned, as in previous systems. Major championship winners will receive 3,000 points, followed by 2,850 for the Players Championship. Winners of PGA Tour Signature events and the first two FedEx Cup playoff tournaments will earn 2,250, while champions at standard full-field Tour events receive 1,500. U.S. players who make the cut and complete those tournaments will also receive points based on their finishing position. Opposite-field events won't count. The top six eligible Americans following the BMW Championship will qualify automatically. Furyk will fill the other six spots on the roster with captain's selections during the week after the Tour Championship. The Americans are trying to win on European soil for the first time since 1993 when they visit Adare Manor in Ireland next September. Furyk said earlier this year that the dramatic changes in PGA Tour purses made prize money a less reliable way to compare performances across different events. The 2027 Ryder Cup will be played Sept. 17-19. --Field Level Media

item.title: Nebraska DL Mac Markway retires due to ongoing knee issues
item.description: Nebraska defensive lineman Mac Markway announced his retirement one game into the new season after battling through knee injuries over the past two years.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Nebraska defensive lineman Mac Markway announced his retirement one game into the new season after battling through knee injuries over the past two years. Markway, who switched from tight end to defensive end this season, posted a statement on his Instagram account Wednesday. He played six snaps in the Cornhuskers' 49-21 win over Ohio on Saturday in Lincoln, Neb., and was listed on the third team of the depth chart for this week's home game against Bowling Green. "The reality is my knees just aren't what they used to be and aren't letting me play at the level I want to," he wrote, citing five season-ending injuries in his football career. "I got a huge weight and stress off my shoulders with this decision and I am truly at peace with it. I am going to be around the facility helping y'all boys in another aspect of football. It's time to conquer the world in a different aspect of not just Mac the football player, but as Mac Markway." Listed at 6-foot-4 and 265 pounds, Markway thanked his teammates and coaches over his career in his social media post. Cornhuskers coach Matt Rhule lauded Markway's comeback from injuries during his Monday news conference. "Mac Markway, coming off of three torn ACLs and been here for two years, hasn't played," Rhule said. "His role will, I think, significantly be amplified each week. I think you'll see him continue to move forward." Markway transferred to Nebraska after his freshman season at LSU, where he played in 12 games with one start in 2023 and caught three passes for 16 yards. He sustained a season-ending torn ACL at Nebraska in 2024 and became a redshirt. Markway's ACL repair failed during fall camp in 2025, causing him to miss the entire season. Markway was selected Academic All-Big Ten in 2025 and made the Nebraska Scholar-Athletic Honor Roll four times. He was a four-star prospect at De Smet Jesuit High School near his native St. Louis, despite missing his senior season while recovering from an injury, according to the Nebraska athletics website. --Field Level Media

item.title: Fachin suspende caso relatado por Mendonça com relatório da PF apontando vínculos de Vorcaro com Moraes, Andrei e Gonet
item.description: O presidente do Supremo Tribunal Federal, Edson Fachin, determinou nesta quarta-feira a suspensão do caso relatado pelo colega André Mendonça em que foi produzido um relatório da Polícia Federal que apontou vínculos do banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro com o colega Alexandre de Moraes, o diretor-geral da PF, Andrei Rodrigues, e o procurador-geral da República, Paulo Gonet.
item.dc:creator: Ricardo Brito
item.content:encoded: O presidente do Supremo Tribunal Federal, Edson Fachin, determinou nesta quarta-feira a suspensão do caso relatado pelo colega André Mendonça em que foi produzido um relatório da Polícia Federal que apontou vínculos do banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro com o colega Alexandre de Moraes, o diretor-geral da PF, Andrei Rodrigues, e o procurador-geral da República, Paulo Gonet. Em 10 páginas de decisão tornada pública, Fachin disse que o plenário deve analisar o caso de forma extraordinária na próxima terça-feira, dia 15 de setembro. Na sua decisão, o presidente do STF deixou claro que é para suspender "todo e qualquer procedimento que verse sobre potencial investigação em face de integrantes deste Supremo Tribunal Federal, os quais devem ser preliminarmente remetidos a esta presidência". O caso relatado por Mendonça, que tornou público na terça-feira da semana passada o teor do relatório da PF de 218 páginas, levou a um grave embate dele com Moraes, que fez um contra-ataque e pediu a investigação do colega por abuso de autoridade e improbidade administrativa. Moraes acusou Mendonça de direcionar alvos das apurações que conduz nos inquéritos do Banco Master e dos desvios de recursos do INSS. Tentando colocar um freio de arrumação na disputa entre os dois, Fachin também ordenou o congelamento do pedido de Moraes contra Mendonça.

item.title: Fight over Republican-drawn congressional map in Missouri returns to US Supreme Court
item.description: Challengers to a redrawn congressional map in Missouri aimed at favoring Republicans asked the U.S. Supreme Court on Wednesday to suspend a federal judge's order that allowed only those reconfigured boundaries to be used in November's midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Chung
item.content:encoded: Challengers to a redrawn congressional map in Missouri aimed at favoring Republicans asked the U.S. Supreme Court on Wednesday to suspend a federal judge's order that allowed only those reconfigured boundaries to be used in November's midterm elections. The map's challengers, including a group opposed to the Republican-drawn map called People Not Politicians, made the request in an emergency filing, moving swiftly after St. Louis, Missouri-based Chief U.S. District Judge Stephen Clark issued his decision on Tuesday. The request brings the fight over Missouri's U.S. House of Representatives districts back to the Supreme Court just one day after it [USN:S0N41Y02P TEXT:"declined"] to intervene in a bid by Missouri officials to reinstate the redrawn map, which the state's top court had blocked until it is put to a referendum. Clark's order appeared to conflict with the Missouri Supreme Court's unanimous September 3 [USN:L1N44V11Z TEXT:"ruling"] blocking the map, leaving the state's congressional districts in limbo and injecting further confusion into the high-stakes electoral fight. Missouri Republicans adopted the new map, which dismantled the Kansas City-based seat of longtime Democratic Representative Emanuel Cleaver, in 2025 as part of a broader effort backed by President Donald Trump to redraw congressional districts in ways that could benefit Republican candidates. Republicans hold a narrow 219-214 majority in the U.S. House, including one independent who caucuses with Republicans. The dispute in Missouri arose when People Not Politicians, which calls itself a coalition of Republicans, Independents, and Democrats opposed to gerrymandering the state's electoral map, collected enough signatures to file for a referendum under a provision in the state constitution that authorizes a ballot measure to approve any legislative act. Hoskins rejected the petition, finding that state constitutional language does not apply to congressional redistricting. The seven-member Missouri Supreme Court, which includes five Republican-appointed judges, disagreed, ruling that the referendum petition was "legal, sufficient, and timely," and that the redrawn map will not take effect until approved by voters. Missouri Republican U.S. Representative Bob Onder and other plaintiffs then filed a lawsuit in federal court seeking to reinstate the Republican-drawn map. In his order on Tuesday, Clark barred the use of any map for the November elections except for the redrawn 2025 map because those congressional district boundaries were already used for the August 4 primary elections. The fight intensified after Republican Secretary of State Denny Hoskins, the state's top election official, responded to Clark's order by telling local election officials to proceed with using the 2025 map. The Missouri Supreme Court then said it would consider holding Hoskins in contempt if it determines he violated its September 3 ruling blocking that map. It ordered him to appear in person on September 10 for a hearing on the matter.

item.title: US trial against China's Huawei opens with prosecutor calling the company a criminal enterprise
item.description: A U.S. prosecutor described China's Huawei as a criminal enterprise that stole from American companies to build its telecommunications empire, as the trial against the tech giant kicked off in Brooklyn federal court on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Karen Freifeld
item.content:encoded: A U.S. prosecutor described China's Huawei as a criminal enterprise that stole from American companies to build its telecommunications empire, as the trial against the tech giant kicked off in Brooklyn federal court on Wednesday. "Theft, lies, cover-up," Taylor Stout, a trial attorney from the U.S. Department of Justice, said in the government's opening statement. "For 20 years, that's how Huawei, a massive Chinese telecommunications company, victimized American companies and abused the American financial system, all in an effort to dominate the telecommunications industry around the world." Huawei conspired to steal trade secrets from five U.S. companies, including operating system source code for internet routers from Cisco Systems (CSCO.O) and a robotic arm to test phones from T-Mobile (TMUS.O) , to gain an unfair competitive advantage and grow its business, the prosecutor told jurors. "We'll hear from people who caught Huawei red-handed trying to steal American tech," Stout said, adding there was video of an employee stealing the robotic arm. The defense painted a very different picture of the company and its success in court. "It's about competition, not conspiracy. Innovation, not theft. Ordinary business dealings, not criminal conduct," Brian Heberlig, one of a team of lawyers representing Huawei, said in his opening. "Huawei earned its success...There was no blueprint for crime." Huawei is known for its telecommunications equipment, mobile phones and, in recent years, AI chips. It does business globally but its networking gear is restricted in the U.S. and suppliers are banned from exporting U.S. goods and technology to the company without approval from the Department of Commerce. DEFENSE SAYS GOVERNMENT 'CHERRY-PICKING' The case against Huawei began in 2018 with an indictment charging the company and its chief financial officer with bank fraud and sanctions violations for allegedly misrepresenting its business in Iran to get around U.S. sanctions and move millions of dollars through the U.S. financial system. In the ensuing years, it grew into a sprawling indictment that includes racketeering, a pattern of illegal activity conducted by an enterprise to generate profit. Heberlig, defending Huawei, told jurors that prosecutors will describe routine activities by global tech companies "but will twist those ordinary activities to try to make them look criminal." The government was "cherry-picking isolated events that should not be viewed as evidence of an overarching conspiracy that never existed," he said. He said the incidents involving Cisco and T-mobile were "actions by individual employees" and that management worked to make things right after learning of them. Another incident in which an employee took unauthorized photos of a Fujitsu networking device at a trade show was a "foolish act" by one employee who was "promptly fired," the defense attorney said. The prosecutor also accused the company of keeping the nature of its work in Iran secret, so it could launder U.S. dollars through the financial system and could help the Iranian government spy on its own citizens. The defense said there was no evidence Huawei knew the dollar-clearing would violate U.S. sanctions law and that the company could have kept it outside the U.S. or in another currency. He also said the banks allegedly misled by Huawei knew about its business in Iran and still competed for its business. In 2018, Huawei's chief financial officer, Meng Wanzhou, was detained in Vancouver after being picked up on a U.S. warrant as a part of the original indictment. She fought extradition for nearly three years before being freed to return to China in a diplomatic agreement between the U.S., China and Canada. The charges against her were dismissed in 2022 as part of a deferred prosecution agreement but admissions she made are set to be introduced as evidence at the trial, which is expected to last three months. The criminal case is based in part on reporting by Reuters in [USN:BRE8BT0BH TEXT:"2012"] and [USN:BRE90U0CC TEXT:"2013"] about close ties between Huawei and Skycom, a firm that operated in Iran. Reuters reported that Skycom had offered to sell at least €1.3 million ($1.5 million) worth of embargoed Hewlett-Packard computer equipment to Iran's largest mobile-phone operator in 2010. Reuters also reported that Meng had served on Skycom's board of directors between February 2008 and April 2009.

item.title: Trump administration alleges UC Berkeley School of Law favors Black applicants in admission
item.description: The U.S. Justice and Education Departments alleged on Wednesday that admissions practices at the University of California, Berkeley School of Law deliberately favored Black applicants and discriminated against white and Asian candidates.
item.dc:creator: Kanishka Singh
item.content:encoded: The U.S. Justice and Education Departments alleged on Wednesday that admissions practices at the University of California, Berkeley School of Law deliberately favored Black applicants and discriminated against white and Asian candidates. A joint probe by the two federal departments whose findings were announced on Wednesday marked the latest [USN:L3N3OP05M TEXT:"crackdown"] on diversity initiatives in universities by President Donald Trump's administration. The administration alleged the UC Berkeley School of Law uses "race, essay prompts, and other tactics to further its admissions diversity goals." Erwin Chemerinsky, dean of the UC Berkeley School of Law, said on Wednesday that the school's "admissions policy is clear that race is not considered in any way in admissions decisions." UC Berkeley's central administration said the university "will spare no effort to provide ample evidence" to show the university complies with all relevant laws, policies and rules governing admissions. Trump, who casts diversity goals as anti-merit and discriminatory against white people and men, has signed orders to dismantle them. Rights advocates say diversity practices address historic inequities for marginalized groups like ethnic minorities, the LGBT community and women. The U.S. Supreme Court rejected affirmative action at colleges in 2023 when it struck down race-conscious admissions programs at Harvard and the University of North Carolina. "The data produced by Berkeley Law demonstrates a strong bias against Asian and white applicants, with a corresponding bias in favor of Black applicants," the Trump administration said, adding Black applicants had 5.8 times higher odds of admission than comparable white applicants in 2025. The law school's October 2025 enrollment data showed 1,128 law students, of whom 516 were white and 293 Asian, with 51 Black students. The Department of Justice said it sought a voluntary resolution agreement with the school. Trump has [USN:L1N44P037 TEXT:"targeted universities"] with probes and funding suspension threats over [USN:L4N3SN13Z TEXT:"pro-Palestinian protests"] against U.S. ally Israel's assault on Gaza, [USN:L3N3OP05M TEXT:"diversity initiatives"], [USN:L4N3R61MM TEXT:"transgender policies"] and climate programs, leading to free speech, due process and academic freedom concerns. His administration has also targeted various other schools over [USN:L4N43O2J4 TEXT:"admissions practices"].

item.title: Rybakina quedará primera en el ranking y Gauff se clasifica para semifinales del Abierto de EEUU
item.description: Elena Rybakina se aseguró de que dejará Flushing Meadows como nueva número uno del mundo tras una contundente victoria sobre Zheng Qinwen en los cuartos de final del Abierto de Estados Unidos este miércoles, mientras que la campeona de 2023, Coco Gauff, se recuperó de un mal comienzo para clasificarse a la semifinal.
item.dc:creator: Amy Tennery
item.content:encoded: Elena Rybakina se aseguró de que dejará Flushing Meadows como nueva número uno del mundo tras una contundente victoria sobre Zheng Qinwen en los cuartos de final del Abierto de Estados Unidos este miércoles, mientras que la campeona de 2023, Coco Gauff, se recuperó de un mal comienzo para clasificarse a la semifinal. La jornada matinal comenzó apenas ocho horas después de que Ben Shelton venció a Carlos Alcaraz en un emocionante partido a cinco sets que terminó a las 3:33 de la madrugada, batiendo el récord del partido que más tarde ha terminado jamás en el Abierto de Estados Unidos. Zheng se había labrado una reputación como una de las mejores jugadoras del torneo a la hora de remontar partidos, pero se quedó sin fuerzas frente a Rybakina y perdió por 3-6, 6-1 y 6-4, mientras la kazaja iba desmontando poco a poco su defensa tras superar sus errores iniciales. "Me cuesta encontrar palabras", dijo Rybakina, que destronó a Aryna Sabalenka en lo más alto de la clasificación. "Quizá no haya sido un partido del más alto nivel, pero me alegro de haberlo superado". Rybakina se enfrentará a la favorita del público estadounidense, Gauff, que tuvo un comienzo desastroso antes de recuperarse y vencer a la quinta cabeza de serie, Mirra Andreeva, por 2-6, 7-6(7) y 6-2. Gauff mejoró notablemente su nivel a lo largo del partido, inspirándose en la remontada de su compatriota Frances Tiafoe, que la noche anterior se había recuperado tras ir perdiendo por dos sets, y salvó dos puntos de partido en el tie-break. Tras el agotador duelo entre Alcaraz y Shelton, que se prolongó hasta la madrugada, los organizadores se prepararán para volver a preparar café extra cuando el cabeza de serie número uno masculino, Alexander Zverev, cierre la sesión nocturna del miércoles frente al holandés Botic van de Zandschulp.

item.title: Estimación cosecha soja de Argentina cae por recorte área: Bolsa Rosario
item.description: La estimación de cosecha para la soja 2026/27 de Argentina cayó en 200.000 toneladas, a 47,8 millones de toneladas, debido a un recorte en la previsión del área que será sembrada por márgenes de rentabilidad del cultivo inferiores a los del maíz, dijo el miércoles la Bolsa de Comercio de Rosario (BCR).
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La estimación de cosecha para la soja 2026/27 de Argentina cayó en 200.000 toneladas, a 47,8 millones de toneladas, debido a un recorte en la previsión del área que será sembrada por márgenes de rentabilidad del cultivo inferiores a los del maíz, dijo el miércoles la Bolsa de Comercio de Rosario (BCR). En cambio, la Bolsa subió su estimación de cosecha para el maíz 26/27 a entre 67,5 y 70,5 millones de toneladas, desde los 66 millones anteriores, gracias a la expansión en las previsiones de siembra. La siembra del maíz 2026/27 comienza en las próximas semanas en Argentina, mientras que la de la soja empieza en octubre. El país sudamericano es el mayor exportador mundial de aceite y harina de soja, y el tercero de maíz. "En la comparación de márgenes, el maíz empieza a ganarle área a la soja", dijo la BCR en su reporte mensual de cultivos. Con respecto al trigo 2026/27, la Bolsa subió en 2,4% su estimación de producción del cereal a 21 millones de toneladas, gracias al buen estado en que se encuentra el cultivo. La siembra del trigo ya terminó en Argentina y la cosecha del cereal comienza en noviembre.

item.title: Trading Day: $100 oil bites
item.description: Stocks around the world fell on Wednesday as entrenched conflict in the Middle East pushed oil prices above $100 a barrel, while bond yields rose to fresh multi-year highs as investors reacted negatively to the U.S. Treasury's plan to triple bond buybacks.
item.dc:creator: Jamie McGeever
item.content:encoded: [USN:L4N4510P8 TEXT:"Stocks"] around the world fell on Wednesday as [USN:L6N45118W TEXT:"entrenched conflict"] in the Middle East pushed oil prices above [USN:P8N43I0BY TEXT:"$100 a barrel"], while bond yields rose to fresh multi-year highs as investors reacted negatively to the U.S. Treasury's plan to triple [USN:L1N4510P7 TEXT:"bond buybacks"]. In [USN:L6N4500TK TEXT:"my column today"], I look at what might replace the Japanese yen as the funding currency of choice in global FX carry trades. Swissie? Loonie? Euro? There's no obvious candidate. Today's Key Reads Iran said on Wednesday it had attacked 10 ships near the Strait of Hormuz after the U.S. sank five Iranian oil tankers, in the [USN:L6N451042 TEXT:"biggest declared wave of tit-for-tat attacks on shipping"] by both sides since the start of the six-month-old war. EXCLUSIVE - AI agents unleashed by OpenAI used more than 10 previously undisclosed websites for unsanctioned communications earlier this year, according to six sets of independent investigators and data reviewed by Reuters, showing that [USN:L6N4510WC TEXT:"the agents’ rogue activity"] was wider ranging than previously disclosed. The United States has banned a broad swath of Canadian alcoholic beverages, motorcycles and dairy products from import, [USN:L6N44W10Z TEXT:"sharply escalating an already acrimonious trade spat."] Even two wars and sky-high energy prices haven't cooled the world economy. Global growth is running hot into the second half of the year, forcing asset managers to find firebreaks while staying invested. Higher interest rates may be the only policy brake left, observes ROI's Mike Dolan . How much oil is flowing through the [USN:L1N44Y067 TEXT:"Strait of Hormuz"]? Traders, energy executives and government officials are all trying to [USN:L1N44A048 TEXT:"figure it out"] — but are reaching wildly different conclusions. It is, however, increasingly clear that this mystery has introduced a residual risk premium into crude prices that could remain deeply entrenched for months. [USN:L6N4500W5 TEXT:"Analysis from ROI's Ron Bousso."] Today's Key Market Moves STOCKS: South Korea outperforms in Asia, +1.3%. [USN:L4N4510FH TEXT:"Europe"] -1.4% to 1-month low. Big three U.S. indices all lower: S&P 500 -0.5%, Nasdaq -0.6%, Dow -0.8%. SECTORS/SHARES: Every sector on the S&P 500 falls, except energy (+1). Industrials -1.5%, utilities -1.2%. [USN:L6N4500XV TEXT:"Meta"] +6.6%, [USN:L6N4510Z3 TEXT:"Apple"] -0.3% on launch of new foldable phone. Comcast -6.6%. FX: [USN:L4N45102E TEXT:"Dollar/yen"] hovers around 7-month low. BONDS: U.S., UK, European yields spike to multi-year highs. The highest U.S. 10-year yield in three years draws strong demand at 10-year auction — bid/cover highest in over a decade, according to Wrightson ICAP. COMMODITIES/METALS: [USN:P8N43I0BY TEXT:"Oil"] marches higher, Brent tops $100/bbl. U.S. diesel at record $5.94/gallon. Today's Talking Points: Our House "I am the house now," U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott [USN:L1N451007 TEXT:"Bessent"] said on Tuesday. "And you can bet against me if you want." Bessent's eye-opening remarks were in reference to his knowledge of, and influence over, the Japanese yen. Remember, the U.S. jointly intervened with Japan to support the yen a few weeks ago. Bessent's swagger here appears to be well-founded — for now at least — with the yen rallying strongly across the board. Of course, time will tell. But it's a different story in the U.S. bond market, where Bessent is even more active, trying to get longer-end yields down. Treasury on Wednesday said it will buy back up to [USN:L1N4510P7 TEXT:"$6 billion of long-dated bonds"] on Thursday, three times its last buyback. But yields leaped to new, historic highs on the announcement. The U.S. bond market is big, there are big bets being made. Again, time will tell. But the house may not always win here. High energy Brent crude oil is back above $100/bbl, WTI isn't far behind and is at a 3-month high. Oil is now up 50% on the same period a year ago. Meanwhile, U.S. gasoline prices are comfortably above $4/gallon, and diesel is at a record $5.94/gallon. War in the Middle East is spreading, and there's little to suggest peace, resolution or ceasefire are anywhere close on the horizon. Puzzling questions from all this are: [USN:L6N4500VT TEXT:"why isn't the economy rolling over"], and will it ever? Of course, the economy is much less energy-intensive now than it was in years gone by, and as we are seeing elsewhere, many traditional macro models, rules of thumb, and correlations have broken down since the COVID-19 pandemic. High energy costs are one of the factors lifting bond yields, and stocks may now be feeling the heat. Are the scales beginning to tip? The fold rush Apple shares have performed reasonably well this year, outperforming all of its "Magnificent 7" peers except Nvidia. Investors have cheered Apple's conservative approach to borrowing — it has eschewed the debt issuance binge many of its peers have undertaken to fund the AI buildout. Apple's market cap briefly topped $5 trillion in July, becoming only the second company to achieve that milestone after Nvidia. But doubts persist around new products and pricing. If the initial share price move on Wednesday following the launch of the company's [USN:L6N4510Z3 TEXT:"foldable phone called "Duo""] is any indication, these doubts aren't lifting any time soon. The cheapest Duo will be $1,999, and that's not cheap. Shares initially fell more than 2% on the unveiling, but recouped most of these losses to end down only 0.3%. That still lagged other Mag 7 and Big Tech stocks, however. What could move markets tomorrow? item.title: AI models’ capabilities leap comes with new safety warnings
item.description: At Goldman Sachs’ annual tech investor gathering, Communacopia + Technology Conference, in San Francisco this week, who wasn’t in the room mattered almost as much as who was.
item.dc:creator: Krystal Hu
item.content:encoded: At Goldman Sachs’ annual tech investor gathering, Communacopia + Technology Conference, in San Francisco this week, who wasn’t in the room mattered almost as much as who was. Investors packed OpenAI CFO [USN:L6N450178 TEXT:"Sarah Friar’s session"], but in the hallways another question kept coming up: Where is Anthropic’s IPO S-1 filing? The company skipped its usual appearance as it prepares for what could be one of the largest IPOs ever. The filing would give investors their first detailed look at how Anthropic’s much-discussed annualized revenue translates into booked GAAP revenue, what its compute costs really look like, and whether private-market valuations can withstand public-market scrutiny. For now, they’ll have to wait a little longer, as the timeline has [USN:L6N44W17K TEXT:"slipped by a few weeks"]. As capital tries to decide just how long the AI boom can keep running, I’ve been trading notes with my colleague Deepa Seetharaman, who has been immersed in a very different corner of the AI world: researchers increasingly worried that the technology is advancing faster than humans can understand or control it. She has been breaking stories on the prime example of that tension — an OpenAI agent that went rogue long before the incident became public, and the company’s decision not to disclose it at the time. So this week, we’re looking at two sides of the same race: investors betting the boom can keep accelerating, and the people building the technology asking whether it should. Scroll on. OUR LATEST REPORTING IN TECH AND AI [USN:L6N45014G TEXT:"Apple shows off iPhone 18 Pro at start of event expected to debut folding phones"] [USN:L6N4510WC TEXT:"OpenAI’s rogue agents used at least 10 more sites for unauthorized comms, researchers say"] [USN:L4N4500M5 TEXT:"China's DeepSeek taps CITIC Securities for domestic IPO, sources say"] [USN:L4N4501G4 TEXT:"Suno releases new AI music models in partnership with Warner Music, BMG"] [USN:L8N44Z0XI TEXT:"Teen reading slumps to worst this century due to surge in screen time"] [USN:S0N4490CN TEXT:"US, China gear up for mid-September AI safety talks"] [USN:L6N44W0BR TEXT:"From dance floor to war: China readies humanoid robots for combat"] THE AI RACE NO ONE CAN AFFORD TO SLOW The past seven days captured the tension defining the AI world right now: frontier models are getting more capable, investors are rewarding the companies building them, yet some of the people closest to those models are getting increasingly alarmed about where the race is heading. Take OpenAI’s new Astra model launched last week. It represents a substantial jump over previous generations. OpenAI employees who are among Astra’s heaviest users burn roughly $7,000 worth of tokens a day, or about $1.5 million a year. Frontier models like Astra also helped train OpenAI’s lighter-weight ones; the company did an 80% price cut on one of those cheaper models and helped [USN:L6N450178 TEXT:"drive a tenfold"] increase in usage. Investors have noticed. Shares in SoftBank, one of OpenAI’s biggest financial backers, have jumped nearly 30% in the past five days as enthusiasm around its AI bets has grown. But as the money celebrates the capability gains, the same advances are setting off alarms elsewhere. Astra arrived amid growing scrutiny of how OpenAI trains and monitors increasingly capable agents. OpenAI’s own system card — the technical report outlining how it tested the model — showed a [USN:L6N44V0KT TEXT:"substantial deterioration"] in so-called monitorability, or researchers’ ability to understand what the model is doing internally. OpenAI said Astra is more likely than earlier models to intentionally conceal or disguise its step-by-step reasoning, making it harder for humans to evaluate how it reached an answer. On more complicated problems, the model is also getting better at covering its tracks. That is particularly uncomfortable given another controversy hanging over the company. Last week, [USN:L6N44W08B TEXT:"Reuters reported exclusively"] that OpenAI knew about a swarm of AI agents targeting a German wiki but did not publicly disclose the incident. A [USN:L6N4510WC TEXT:"follow-up investigation shows"] AI agents launched by OpenAI used at least 10 previously undisclosed websites for unsanctioned communications earlier this year. OpenAI said it did not disclose the case because it was similar to other incidents it had already made public. Taken together, the developments are unsettling some researchers who say capability gains are arriving faster than they expected, even as humans have less visibility into — and potentially less control over — how the models operate. The German wiki case raises a separate but related question: how much should the public trust the companies building these systems to police themselves when greater capability may come at the expense of monitorability? That concern is increasingly coming from inside the labs themselves. Even OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki has suggested that leading labs should be willing to coordinate a voluntary slowdown if needed to build confidence in their safety measures. Other OpenAI researchers have expressed similar ideas. Aidan Clark wrote that, for the first time, he was asking himself whether “things are moving too fast.” Boaz Barak said employees were beginning to feel “viscerally the magnitude of capabilities” and “there are also many ways it can end up very badly.” Anthropic has positioned itself as the more safety-conscious frontier lab, but is not immune to these concerns. This week, its researcher Jacob Coxon, who previously worked at OpenAI, resigned and accused both companies of racing toward self-improving superintelligence without acting responsibly. Some employees at both labs would like their leaders to reach an agreement on when and how to slow down. But that runs into a practical problem: there is [USN:L6N42D13P TEXT:"deep distrust "]between OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei. There is also an enormous amount of money riding on staying ahead. Anthropic is gearing up for the largest public listing in history that could value it at an astounding $2 trillion. OpenAI, meanwhile, needs financing to pay for the compute required to keep pushing its models forward. Every new capability can help justify the next funding round, infrastructure commitment or IPO. That leaves the frontier labs caught in several races at once: to build the most capable model, secure enough compute to train the next one, and reach the public markets before their rivals. The people actually building these systems are increasingly asking whether the pace itself has become a problem, and whether the trade-off between capability and control is becoming too dangerous. The harder question is whether anyone in the race can afford to be the first to slow down. CHART OF THE WEEK AI agents from OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta going rogue didn’t just alarm researchers. They also highlighted how quickly the cyber-risk landscape is changing for companies and insurers. Reported AI incidents have shifted sharply over the past decade: maliciously driven incidents now account for a much larger share of failures, while incidents tied primarily to system safety, failures and limitations have declined as a share of the total. As the industry is still learning what increasingly autonomous models can do, insurers are being asked to price risks that are evolving faster than the policy language designed to cover them. Insurers including MSIG and Beazley are taking notice, my colleagues [USN:L6N44A125 TEXT:"wrote"]. Insurance companies are reviewing traditional cyber policies and adjusting language to account for risks from more autonomous AI systems: agents that can escape controlled environments, take actions without direct human instruction and potentially carry out cyberattacks. That raises basic questions about whether an autonomous AI system fits traditional definitions of a cyber attacker and who is liable when an AI-generated action causes a loss.

item.title: 10-year yields highest since 2023
item.description: Benchmark 10-year Treasury yields reached their highest levels since 2023 on Wednesday after the announcement of an enlarged Treasury buyback of longer-dated bonds disappointed some investors who had wanted more.
item.dc:creator: Karen Brettell, Sinead Carew
item.content:encoded: Benchmark 10-year Treasury yields reached their highest levels since 2023 on Wednesday after the announcement of an enlarged Treasury buyback of longer-dated bonds disappointed some investors who had wanted more. Yields retreated from their highs, however, after the Treasury saw very strong demand for a $39 billion sale of 10-year notes. The [USN:L1N4510PH TEXT:"U.S. Treasury Department"] said it will buy up to $6 billion in 10- to 20-year Treasury bonds during its buyback operation on Thursday, triple the size of its last long-dated operation. "People thought the buyback was going to be larger than $6 billion. It was a disappointment so bond prices sank and yields rose," said Tom di Galoma, managing director at Mischler Financial. After a selloff that pushed 30-year yields to their highest level since 2007, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced in August that the government would increase buybacks of longer-dated bonds. Very strong demand for a 10-year note auction then brought yields off this highs, with the debt selling at the highest yield since 2007. "The auction came at a historical high for 2026 and buyers showed up with very strong demand. The reason they showed up in a very large way is because tomorrow the Treasury is going to buy 10-year to 20-year paper. Investors may have thought it was a risk-free trade," di Galoma said. Treasury Department sold the 10-year notes at a high yield of 4.834%, more than a basis point below where they traded ahead of the auction. Demand was 2.71 times the amount of debt on offer, the highest since 2019. The U.S. government already saw solid demand for its $58 billion sale of 3-year notes on Tuesday and will also sell $22 billion in 30-year bonds on Thursday. The yield on benchmark U.S. 10-year notes was last up 3.06 basis points at 4.835% after earlier reaching 4.8568%, the highest level since November 2023. The 30-year bond yield rose 2.06 basis points to 5.2846% after touching its highest level since August 18. The 2-year note yield, which typically moves in step with interest rate expectations for the Federal Reserve, rose 2.52 basis points to 4.423%, after earlier trading at 4.4316%, its highest level since July 2024. A closely watched part of the U.S. Treasury yield curve measuring the gap between yields on two- and 10-year Treasury notes, seen as an indicator of economic expectations, was at a positive 41.0 basis points. Meanwhile, oil prices breached $100 for the first time since July as the intensifying conflict in the Middle East heightened concerns about supply. The move came as investors waited for inflation data, which analysts say will be key to the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision next week. "The inflationary story is getting a little stickier, and that could cause the Fed to hike rates," said Lawrence Gillum, chief fixed income strategist for LPL Financial in Fort Mill, South Carolina. FED POLICYMAKERS MEET NEXT WEEK U.S. producer price and consumer price inflation reports are due to be released on Thursday and Friday, respectively. And analysts said the data will play a key role in whether the Fed hikes rates at its September 15-16 meeting. Rising oil prices have reignited concerns that higher fuel costs will flow through to consumer inflation and add to inflation that is already running above the U.S. central bank's 2% annual target. Traders raised bets on a rate hike at the Fed's meeting next week after the Labor Department reported on Friday that employers added [USN:L1N44W0EC TEXT:"far more positions"] than expected in August. Fed funds futures traders are now pricing in about 60% odds of a rate hike next week.

item.title: Gauff fights back to beat Andreeva and reach US Open semis
item.description: American Coco Gauff saved two match points to beat Russian fifth seed Mirra Andreeva 2-6 7-6(7) 6-2 on Wednesday and reach the U.S. Open semi-finals after recovering from a dreadful opening set.
item.dc:creator: Amy Tennery
item.content:encoded: American Coco Gauff saved two match points to beat Russian fifth seed Mirra Andreeva 2-6 7-6(7) 6-2 on Wednesday and reach the U.S. Open semi-finals after recovering from a dreadful opening set. The 2023 champion had none of her usual firepower at first and was on the ropes in the tiebreak before she flipped the script and closed out the match with a forehand strike, dropping her racket to the court in joy and relief. She faces second seed Elena Rybakina in the last four. "The motto of the match was just to fight," said Gauff. Andreeva looked completely at home in Arthur Ashe Stadium as she sprinted through the first four games, never allowing Gauff to set up a break-point chance in the opening set where the Russian had just five unforced errors to 14 from her opponent. Gauff, who took a break in the locker room between sets, took inspiration from her compatriot Frances Tiafoe, who recovered from two sets and a break down on Tuesday night to reach the semi-finals on the men's side. "I just had to reset. I came out not feeling the ball, giving her too many free points," said Gauff. "I was thinking about Frances Tiafoe and how he came back yesterday. And we all want to do well in front of this crowd." Gauff finally found some momentum in the second set and was serving for the match in the ninth game when old issues with her serve resurfaced and she produced three double faults, allowing her opponent to break back. Undeterred, Gauff recovered her poise and deployed a perfectly placed backhand to win a 39-shot rally, twice saving match point before forcing the third set with a forehand shot to the corner that Andreeva could not contain. She kept up the pace from there and Andreeva flung her racket at her bench in disgust after dropping her serve in the third game of the decider. Gauff broke her to love in the seventh game to put the contest completely out of reach. She faces a formidable foe in Rybakina, who claimed the top ranking with a [USN:L6N45118I TEXT:"win earlier in the day"] over Zheng Qinwen. Gauff and the Kazakh second seed have one win apiece in career head-to-head, with Rybakina winning their most recent encounter in the semi-finals in Toronto last month. "Elena - she's the new world number one so it's going to be a tough match," said Gauff. "I'm looking forward to the battle. These are the moments you live for."

item.title: Oklahoma judge used AI in ruling that contained false citations, prosecutor says
item.description: An Oklahoma judge has acknowledged that a ruling he issued contained fictitious citations generated by artificial intelligence, according to state records, adding to a growing number of cases in which judges have faced scrutiny over AI use.
item.dc:creator: Mike Scarcella
item.content:encoded: An Oklahoma judge has acknowledged that a ruling he issued contained fictitious citations generated by artificial intelligence, according to state records, adding to a growing number of cases in which judges have faced scrutiny over AI use. The judge, Lawrence Wheeler of the District Court of Stephens County, told an investigator with the Oklahoma State Bureau of Investigation that he used OpenAI’s ChatGPT for research, and that an order he drafted contained two citations to cases that do not exist, according to an August 17 letter from a prosecutor to the state attorney general's office. Wheeler, who was elected in 2022 and presides over a family law docket, did not immediately respond to a request for comment left with his office in Duncan, Oklahoma. His lawyer, Scott Anderson, said in a statement that “Judge Wheeler and I have no comment on the matter at this time.” Wheeler's use of AI was included in a judicial misconduct complaint that also alleged that the judge secretly listened to jury deliberations, county district attorney Jason Hicks said in the letter, which was reviewed by Reuters. The Oklahoman newspaper first reported the letter. The Oklahoma Attorney General’s Office in a statement on Wednesday said it reviewed the allegations but the evidence was insufficient to prosecute. The office said the Oklahoma Supreme Court and another state judicial body have power to discipline judges whether or not there is a criminal violation. The growing use of AI technology in the courts and at law firms has put new scrutiny on the accuracy of filings and orders, stemming from instances where AI has made up case citations or misquoted the law. Two federal judges last year said the use of AI in their chambers [USN:L1N3W40R4 TEXT:"led to errors"] in two court rulings. A Georgia [USN:L6N41I0SY TEXT:"prosecutor’s use of AI"] led to erroneous citations appearing in a ruling in a murder case. OpenAI did not immediately respond to a request for comment. According to the August 17 letter, Hicks recused himself from investigating Wheeler and asked Oklahoma State Attorney General Gentner Drummond to review the Oklahoma State Bureau of Investigation's report or reassign the inquiry. Drummond’s office in its statement on Wednesday said its criminal division “thoroughly reviewed” the claims and was not pursuing them further. The Oklahoma Council on Judicial Complaints in a statement on Wednesday said it cannot comment on or confirm any investigation. The Oklahoma Supreme Court did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
